title: TexasAM vs UTAustin: tuition, size, accreditation
summary: University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center (TexasAM) versus The University of Texas at Austin (UTAustin). Also searched as UTAustin vs TexasAM. Scorecard table is sourced; prose is checked against those facts. UniRepository is not affiliated with either school.

sections.heading: How they differ
paragraphs: The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center and The University of Texas at Austin are both public institutions located in Texas, but they differ significantly in their focus and student populations. UT Southwestern, based in Dallas, primarily serves as a medical center and does not have an undergraduate enrollment, reflecting its specialized graduate and professional programs. In contrast, The University of Texas at Austin, situated in Austin, has a substantial undergraduate enrollment of 42,855 students. Additionally, UT Austin's in-state tuition is $11,688, a figure not applicable to UT Southwestern due to its distinct academic structure.

sections.heading: Cost
paragraphs: The University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center and The University of Texas at Austin differ notably in their cost structures due to their distinct academic missions. UT Southwestern, focused on graduate and professional medical education, does not have traditional undergraduate tuition rates, whereas UT Austin charges an in-state tuition of $11,688. For out-of-state students, UT Austin's tuition is significantly higher at $44,908. Additionally, the median debt for students completing their education at UT Austin is approximately $20,500, a figure not reported for UT Southwestern. These differences reflect the unique nature of each institution's programs and student demographics.
